name: earthquake
job: Rank 250 m Neighborhoods by the chance that buildings were damaged, from NISAR coherence, displacement and backscatter change
user: Search-and-rescue and damage-assessment teams deciding where to look first

labels.source: Copernicus EMS EMSR884 building damage grades: EMSR884_AOI02_GRA_MONIT01_v2, EMSR884_AOI02_GRA_PRODUCT_v1, EMSR884_AOI12_GRA_MONIT01_v3, EMSR884_AOI12_GRA_MONIT02_v1, EMSR884_AOI12_GRA_PRODUCT_v2
labels.notes: Positive = any building graded Damaged or Destroyed. Neighborhoods with only 'Possibly damaged' buildings are left out. Negatives are analysed areas with no graded building, which includes empty land.

baseline.name: Mean coherence loss across the event (best threshold)

split: Spatial 5-fold cross-validation over 5 km blocks (142 damaged, 1327 undamaged Neighborhoods); scores are out-of-fold
limits: Labels cover only the Caraballeda coast and part of Caracas; elsewhere in the site the map is an extrapolation
Copernicus mapped damage from optical imagery; buildings hidden by roofs or cloud are missed, so some 'undamaged' Neighborhoods are not
NISAR coherence is 80 m, coarser than single buildings: the Model finds damaged areas, not damaged buildings
Only 142 damaged Neighborhoods: scores move by about 0.1 between block layouts, so the gain over the Baseline is modest
